extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent practitioners preparing U.S. national-stage (PCT) filings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for entering the United States national stage from a PCT (international) application under 35 U.S.C. 371 and related 37 CFR provisions. Covers timing, required documents and fees, translations, claim/amendment format, fees for late submissions, and consequences of non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submissions under 35 U.S.C. 371(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall file in the Patent and Trademark Office: (1) the national fee provided in section 41(a); (2) a copy of the international application, and a translation into English if filed in another language; (3) amendments to the claims made under PCT Article 19, and English translation if made in another language; (4) an oath or declaration of the inventor complying with section 115 and relevant regulations; (5) an English translation of any annexes to the international preliminary examination report if made in another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are the core documents/fees required to commence and fulfill the U.S. national stage; some may be waived or postponed under specified conditions (see specific entries below). Failure to comply by required times is treated as abandonment unless unavoidable and shown to the Director's satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage commencement timing (generally 30 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to 35 U.S.C. 371(f), the national stage shall commence with the expiration of the applicable PCT time limit (PCT Articles 22(1)/(2) or 39(1)(a)), typically 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent an express request for early processing under 35 U.S.C. 371(f) (and compliance with its conditions), commencement is at 30 months. See 37 CFR 1.491(a) and related MPEP discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into the national stage (37 CFR 1.491 / 1.495)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application enters the national stage when the applicant has filed the documents and fees required by 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1) and (c)(2) within the period set in 37 CFR 1.495. For pre-AIA applications, analogous pre-AIA paragraphs apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry is distinct from commencement; entry requires timely filing of the required documents/fees within the statutory/ regulatory periods. See differences noted for international filing dates before vs on/after Sept. 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fulfillment of 35 U.S.C. 371
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application fulfills the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371 when the national stage has commenced under 35 U.S.C. 371(b) or (f) and all applicable requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371 have been satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fulfillment is a legal condition affecting examination and publication; ensure all applicable subsections are satisfied per 37 CFR 1.491(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to timely comply (abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with required submissions (e.g., national fee, copy, translations, oath) by the applicable deadlines shall be regarded as abandonment of the application as to the United States unless unavoidable and satisfactorily shown to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thirty-month deadline may not be extended. Certain omissions may trigger notices and limited correction periods (see paragraph (c) procedures), but failure to timely correct will result in abandonment. Specific non-extendable rules apply to payment of the basic national fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions required by 30 months to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid abandonment, not later than 30 months from the priority date the applicant must furnish: (1) a copy of the international application (unless previously communicated or filed in USPTO), and (2) the basic national fee (see § 1.492(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these are timely filed before 30 months, the Office will notify any omitted items (e.g., English translation, inventor’s oath/declaration, search fee, examination fee, application size fee) and set a period to provide them. The inventor’s oath/declaration may, under conditions, be postponed until the application is in condition for allowance (post-AIA rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office notification and cure periods for omitted items
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant complies with the basic submission before 30 months, the Office will notify the applicant of omitted items (translation, oath, search fee, examination fee, size fee) and set a time period within which the applicant must provide them to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time set is typically 2 months from notification or 32 months from priority date, whichever is later; pre-AIA rules allowed extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Certain fees (processing/surcharge) apply to late acceptance (see late fees entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and verification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A translation into English of the international application (if filed in another language) and of any annexes to the international preliminary examination report must be furnished by deadlines (generally by commencement or within a set cure period). Verification of translations may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations not timely received are considered canceled. Processing fee is required for acceptance of an English translation later than 30 months (see § 1.492(i)). For sequence listings and XML specifics, see separate sequence-listing entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing translation rule (post July 1, 2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications having an international filing date on or after July 1, 2022, an English translation is required for any Sequence Listing XML containing non-English language values for language-dependent free text qualifiers (per §§ 1.831–1.834).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For filing dates before July 1, 2022, a sequence listing need not be translated if it complies with PCT Rule 12.1(d) and the description complies with PCT Rule 5.2(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 19 amendments filed with the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of an international application may be amended under PCT Article 19 (description and drawings may not). Article 19 amendments (including a complete claim set in English) will be entered by replacing original English claims; if made in another language, applicant must provide an English translation by commencement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 19 amendments not received by commencement are considered canceled (35 U.S.C. 371(d)). If canceled but desired, they must be offered as preliminary or responsive amendments under 37 CFR 1.121 or 1.111. Form PTO-1390 includes a checkbox to instruct the U.S. DO/EO not to enter Article 19 amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 34 amendments / annexes (international preliminary examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments properly made under PCT Article 34 during the international preliminary examination (annexed to the IPER) will be annexed and communicated to elected Offices; English annexes are normally entered into the U.S. national stage application unless applicant directs otherwise or entry would cause inconsistencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If annexes are in a foreign language, an English translation must be furnished by 30 months (or within the cure period set by 37 CFR 1.495(c) accompanied by processing fee § 1.492(f)) or they will be canceled. Translations must allow substitution of translated pages without causing inconsistencies; if entry would cause inconsistencies, annexes will not be entered (Form PCT/DO/EO/903 will indicate non-entry). Amendments introducing new matter must be handled by examiner as in regular U.S. applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment format and required claim-status listing
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending claims in the national phase, follow 37 CFR 1.121 and 1.125: include a complete listing of all claims ever presented with the status of every claim indicated in a parenthetical expression (Original, Currently Amended, Canceled, Withdrawn, Previously Presented, New, Not Entered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All 'currently amended' claims must include markings (underlining for additions; strike-through or double brackets for deletions) relative to the immediate prior version. The Office may waive certain provisions and accept alternative status identifiers (see MPEP § 714 II.C.E). Noncompliant proposed amendments will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status-identifier specifics for claims entered from PCT amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'original' for claims presented on the international filing date and not modified; use 'previously presented' for claims added/modified under PCT Articles 19 or 34 that were entered in the national phase; use 'canceled' for claims canceled under PCT amendment that were entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP provides concrete examples illustrating claim-status labeling in various Article 19/34 scenarios (examples 1–4). Proper identification avoids confusion and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application identification to be used in communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a U.S. application number has been accorded to the national-stage application, that U.S. application number should be used whenever papers or communications are directed to the USPTO regarding the national stage application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the U.S. application number expedites processing (Patent Data Portal tracks via the eight-digit U.S. application number). Also include international application number, international filing date, and national stage entry date to cross-check a possibly erroneous U.S. application number.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States as Designated or Elected Office and entry route
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will act as Designated Office (DO/US) or Elected Office (EO/US) for international applications designating/electing the U.S.; an international application designating the U.S. will enter via the DO unless a Demand electing the U.S. is filed under PCT Article 31, whereupon entry will be via the EO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major DO/EO functions include receiving notifications during international stage and national stage processing. When entering following Chapter I or II, the applicant has the right to amend within one month from commencement (PCT Art. 28/41; PCT Rules 52.1/78.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible filing methods and mailing rules for national-stage submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is preferable to file required national stage items online using the USPTO patent electronic filing system (EFS). Applicants may also use Priority Mail Express; facsimile transmission is not acceptable for submission of the basic national fee and/or the copy of the international application. Certificate of mailing procedures (37 CFR 1.8) do not apply to filing the copy and basic fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the EFS for faster processing; see USPTO website for filing information. Failure to follow acceptable filing methods may jeopardize timely receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late filing: processing fees and surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: A processing fee (§ 1.492(i)) is required for acceptance of an English translation later than the expiration of thirty months after the priority date. A surcharge (§ 1.492(h)) is required for acceptance of any of the search fee, examination fee, or inventor’s oath/declaration after the date of commencement. Applicants cannot pay the basic national fee with a surcharge after the 30-month deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different pre-AIA vs post-AIA rules govern what may be postponed and what fees apply. Timely compliance avoids additional fees and risk of abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-commencement treatment of amendments and patent grant/refusal timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After an international application has entered the national stage, no patent may be granted or refused thereon before the expiration of the applicable time limit under PCT Article 28 or Article 41, except with the express consent of the applicant. The applicant may present amendments to the specification, claims, and drawings after the national stage has commenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants retain the right to amend during national stage; however, Article 34 amendments made after commencement are not considered in the U.S. national stage and must be submitted as U.S. amendments (e.g., preliminary amendment under 37 CFR 1.121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of amendments that introduce new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry of an amendment made during the international phase into the national stage application does not permit introduction of new matter; where an amendment is determined to introduce new matter, the examiner should require removal and make necessary rejections as in regular U.S. national applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PCT Article 34(2)(b) and MPEP §§ 608.04 and 2163.06 for examiner procedures when new matter is present in amendments entered from PCT documents.
